'''Fritz-Albert Popp''' (11 May 1938 – 4 August 2018<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.life-energy.institute/default.html |title=International Institute of Life Energy |website=www.life-energy.institute |access-date=2019-10-11}}</ref>) was a German researcher in [[biophysics]], particularly in the study of [[biophoton]]s.<ref name="Champagne2009">{{cite book|last=Champagne|first=C. S. K. Mishra, Pascale|title=Biotechnology Applications|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5VZyADqBbxYC&pg=PA363|accessdate=16 August 2012|date=2009-01-01|publisher=I. K. International Pvt Ltd|isbn=978-93-80026-29-9|pages=363–}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Popp was born in 1938 in Frankfurt. He has a diploma in Experimental Physics (1966, [[University Würzburg]]), a  Ph.D. in Theoretical Physics (1969, [[University Mainz]]), and a [[habilitation]] in Biophysics and Medicine (1973, University Marburg).<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Bischof|first=Marco|date=2008-06-01|title=A tribute to Fritz-Albert Popp on the occasion of his 70th birthday|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/23165441|journal=Indian Journal of Experimental Biology|volume=46|issue=5|pages=267–72|pmid=18697611}}</ref> He was awarded Professorship (H2) by the Senate of Marburg University, and lectured at [[Marburg University]] from 1973 to 1980.<ref name=":0" />

In the mid-1970s, Popp rediscovered and made the first extensive physical analysis of [[biophoton]]s (they were originally discovered in 1922).<ref name=":0" /> 

He was head of a research group in the pharmaceutical industry in Worms from 1981 to 1983 and head of a research group at the Institute of Cell Biology ([[University of Kaiserslautern]]) from 1983 to 1986 and of another research group at the Technology Center in [[Kaiserslautern]]. Popp became an Invited Member and of the [[New York Academy of Sciences]] and an Invited Foreign Member of the Russian Academy of Natural Sciences (RANS). 

Popp is the founder of the International Institute of Biophysics in [[Neuss]] (1996), Germany, an international network of 19 research groups from 13 countries involved in [[biophoton]] research and coherence systems in biology.<ref name="Rattemeyer Popp Nagl 1981 pp. 572–573">{{cite journal | last1=Rattemeyer | first1=M. | last2=Popp | first2=F. A. | last3=Nagl | first3=W. | title=Evidence of photon emission from DNA in living systems | journal=Naturwissenschaften | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=68 | issue=11 | year=1981 | issn=0028-1042 | doi=10.1007/bf00401671 | pages=572–573| pmid=7322208 | bibcode=1981NW.....68..572R | s2cid=35614197 }}</ref><ref name="Popp Li Gu 1992 p.
